notes: WebSearch's shared session budget was exhausted before any query for this scout ran (0 of 4 planned queries executed). Fell back to WebFetch on DuckDuckGo (blocked at connection level, ECONNREFUSED), then Bing (pages rendered but consistently omitted github.com results even for exact-match queries that gh confirms have hits — Bing's site:github.com results appear to be JS-paginated and not present in the fetched HTML), then plain github.com/search (HTTP 429, 1hr backoff) and google.com/search (JS shell, no results). Ended up relying primarily on `gh search repos` (used all 4 allowed calls) plus a modest number of `gh api search/repositories` calls (same read-only public GitHub search endpoint, used because every text-search avenue specified in the brief was non-functional in this session) to actually surface repositories, then verified promising ones with gh api contents/readme calls. Net effect: coverage of GitHub is solid for this theme, but coverage of non-GitHub hosts (Kaggle, Zenodo, Dataverse, HuggingFace, awesome-lists, blog posts) that the brief also asked for is weak, since those require working web search/fetch that was not available. A very large number of hits (Mexico City, Rio, Buenos Aires, Santiago, Bogota, Medellin, Sao Paulo, Lima) are near-identical student EDA/ML-pricing notebooks that load a single Inside-Airbnb-style CSV and add nothing new — excluded per brief. No LatAm-specific STR regulation tracker, no AirDNA/Key Data/Transparent LatAm sample export, no DATATUR/Embratur/IBGE/INEGI tourism-volume GitHub mirror, and no FIFA World Cup 2026 host-city (Mexico City included) events dataset were found on GitHub despite targeted queries — these remain real gaps. Two committed-data finds are worth a second look by someone with a working search tool: DanielDaCosta/airbnb-analysis (Rio, Jan2010-Jan2020 listings+reviews zips, ~69MB total, a genuinely old vintage) and rodolfopardo/Airbnb-Buenos-Aires (a 3MB listings.csv built for an Infobae Económico piece, ~2019-2020 vintage). Suggest a future scout on this theme get a working WebSearch budget and try Kaggle/Zenodo/HuggingFace directly rather than site:github.com queries.

candidates.name: airbnb-analysis (DanielDaCosta)
candidates.what_it_holds: CSV/listings.zip (28.0MB) and CSV/reviews.zip (40.8MB) committed in-repo: detailed Airbnb listings and reviews data for Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, spanning January 2010 to January 2020 per the README (an Inside-Airbnb-style detailed export, not just a single-month snapshot). Jupyter notebook Data_Analysis.ipynb walks through geographic pricing, host response rate vs. score, YoY growth, and price vs. accommodates. MIT-unspecified license (none declared), last commit 2022-04-08, 5 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Rio de Janeiro is not in our current 13-city Inside Airbnb panel, and this vintage (2010-2020) predates anything reachable off today's Inside Airbnb CDN — directly matches gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb-style dumps) for a LatAm market, and could support gap #2 (realised occupancy/ADR) if the detailed listings file carries price/review-based occupancy proxies over a full decade.
candidates.license: none declared (repo has a LICENSE file but type not confirmed)

candidates.name: Airbnb-Buenos-Aires (rodolfopardo)
candidates.what_it_holds: A single committed listings.csv (3.14MB) of Buenos Aires Airbnb listings, described as prepared for a data-journalism piece for Infobae Económico (Argentine outlet). Repo dated 2020, 0 stars, no further documentation visible in the file listing beyond the CSV.
candidates.why_useful: Buenos Aires is not in our current 13-city Inside Airbnb panel; a ~2019-2020 listings snapshot would be an older vintage than anything on the current CDN and gives a starting point for a LatAm market outside our coverage, though it is a single cross-section (no calendar/price-over-time) so value is modest.

candidates.name: Airbnb-Buenos-Aires (gemorenov42)
candidates.what_it_holds: Single large Jupyter notebook (~11.99MB, 'Microproyecto_1_Aprendizaje_No_Supervisado...ipynb') described as 'Base de datos obtenida de Airbnb Inside [sic], con datos de propiedades de Buenos Aires, Argentina'. No separate CSV visible in the top-level file listing; data likely embedded as notebook output cells or pulled at runtime from Inside Airbnb. Updated 2026-09-04 (very recent), 0 stars.
candidates.why_useful: If the embedded data is a fresh (Sep 2026) Inside Airbnb pull for Buenos Aires, it would be a current vintage for a city outside our 13-city panel; unconfirmed without opening the notebook cell outputs.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: possible duplicate of official Inside Airbnb Buenos Aires dump if that is its source; unverified

candidates.name: airbnb_webscraping (hucodelab)
candidates.what_it_holds: A small scraper described as performing 'web scraping of airbnb in Sao Paulo - BR'. 1 star, last updated 2022-06-25. Method/tooling repo, not a stored dataset; not run per CLAUDE.md rule 6 (scraping airbnb.com directly is a terms-of-service decision for a human).
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates that Sao Paulo listing-level scraping code exists publicly, but it scrapes airbnb.com directly, which is outside our sanctioned-source list; catalogued as a method only, left unrun.

candidates.name: airdna-api (guestready)
candidates.what_it_holds: A small client library/wrapper for the AirDNA API (2 stars, updated 2026-01-27). Not LatAm-specific and not a stored dataset; would require an AirDNA API key (paid) to pull anything, so it is a method pointer only.
candidates.why_useful: AirDNA is the highest-value named source for gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs); this client shows the API is programmatically reachable, though a paid key is required and none is authorized for this project.

candidates.name: airdna (api-evangelist)
candidates.what_it_holds: An independent third-party documentation/profile of the AirDNA Enterprise API surface (market metrics, STR listing data, comparable sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates) covering 10M+ listings across 120,000+ markets globally, including LatAm markets. No data committed, just an API surface description; updated 2026-09-13 (very recent).
candidates.why_useful: Useful as a map of what AirDNA's paid API actually exposes (relevant to gap #2) if the team ever gets a licensed key; not itself a dataset and not LatAm-specific.

candidates.name: Airbnb-in-Mexico-City (bernardorosalesromero3-web)
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of Airbnb CDMX listings (2023 vintage per description) focused on geographic distribution, price structure, commercial-host proliferation, and housing-market pressure tied to the gentrification debate. Framing is explicitly regulatory/gentrification-adjacent, but data source appears to be the standard Inside Airbnb Mexico City export we already hold; 0 stars.
candidates.why_useful: The framing (commercial-host share, gentrification pressure) is closer to a regulatory angle than a pure pricing notebook, but without a distinct or older dataset it likely duplicates data we already hold for Mexico City.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: likely duplicates our held Inside Airbnb Mexico City vintages
